case_title: Gurmail Singh v. State of Punjab
accused_victim_relationship: Prior enmity/dispute: accused annoyed with victim's family over teasing of Nindo (daughter of accused Sher Singh); neighbours living close together in same locality
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302 r/w s.149; IPC s.302; IPC s.324 r/w s.149; IPC s.323 r/w s.149
weapon: Knives (kirch) and lathis; a dang blow was also struck
evidence_type: Eyewitness (injured eyewitnesses); medical (injury examination and post-mortem by Dr. O.P. Agarwal)
aggravating_circumstances: Armed group of accused raised a lalkara threatening retribution; fatal knife injury deep into stomach (vital part); several injuries caused to the second victim
trial_court_outcome: Convicted Gurnam Singh, Gurmail Singh, Gurcharan Singh and Sher Singh of murder of Baljinder Singh; acquitted four others. Sentence not stated
high_court_outcome: Affirmed the trial court's judgment (convictions upheld)
offence_finally_established: Murder (IPC s.302 r/w s.149) for the accused other than Sher Singh, who was acquitted
neutral_facts: On 25 March 1996, a group of related men from one family, who lived close together in the same locality, gathered at a house and drank liquor to celebrate a family marriage proposal. Around 1 p.m. they came into the street and raised a challenge that they would teach a neighbouring family a lesson for having teased a daughter of one of the men. Some were armed with small knives and others with lathis. A member of the victim's family came out to persuade them not to abuse and to settle the dispute the next morning. Two other members of the victim's family then arrived. The men shouted that the victim's side should not be allowed to live. One man stabbed the victim on the right side of the abdomen. When a second family member came forward to help, another man stabbed him below the chest, and a third man stabbed him on the lower right flank. That injured man fell, and another man struck him on the right shoulder with a blunt weapon. Women from the families then threw bricks, and the attackers ran from the spot. The victim and the injured man were taken to a hospital in a truck, and the victim died on the way. A doctor who examined the injured man at the initial stage declared him unfit to make a statement. A doctor conducted the post-mortem and recorded a small red abrasion on the right shoulder region, which was attributed to one of the men said to be carrying a lathi. The fatal stomach wound was deep and caused death within a short time.
physical_harm: Death of Baljinder Singh from deep knife wound to the stomach; Rajwinder Singh injured by knife blows to the right side below the chest and right flank and a dang blow to the right shoulder
number_of_offences: 4 charged; 1 finally upheld (s.302 r/w s.149 murder, for accused other than Sher Singh)
premeditation_planning: Not expressly found. Court noted accused drank together and then came out armed after raising a lalkara threatening retribution
motive: Annoyance over the victim family's teasing of Nindo, daughter of accused Sher Singh
key_evidence_accepted: Eyewitness account of the injured eyewitness (Rajwinder Singh) and medical evidence of the fatal stomach injury and the injury attributed to Sher Singh
post_offence_conduct: Accused ran away from the spot after women hurled brickbats (as described in the facts; not separately assessed by the court)
trial_duration: offence: 25 March 1996; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 19.01.2007; Supreme Court: 20 April 2011
legal_representation: Mr. D.P. Singh argued for the accused/appellants; P.N. Puri, Manu Sharma, Sanjay Jain, Avneet Toor and Kuldip Singh listed for the appearing parties; State counsel not named
investigation_status: Investigation completed; eight accused brought to trial
appeal_history: Trial court: 4 convicted, 4 acquitted. High Court: affirmed. Supreme Court: Sher Singh's appeal allowed (acquitted); other appeals dismissed
prosecution_argument: Supported the trial court's judgment; the injuries and common intention established murder
defence_argument: Offence was culpable homicide not amounting to murder (s.304 Part I); s.34 not made out; Sher Singh's injury could have come from a scuffle and was not possible with a lathi
legal_principle_applied: Clause thirdly of s.300 IPC (intention to cause the very injury), tested by objective satisfaction of the court; common intention under s.34/149 from prior enmity, armed group and lalkara
precedent_relied_upon: Virsa Singh v. State of Punjab AIR 1958 SC 465; Laxman Karlu Nikalje v. State of Maharashtra (1968) 3 SCR 685; Harjinder Singh v. Delhi Administration AIR 1968 SC 867; Randhir Singh v. State of Punjab (1981) 4 SCC 484; Tholan v. State of Tamil Nadu (1984) 2 SCC 133; Arun Nivalaji More v. State of Maharashtra (2006) 2 SCC 613
judicial_aggravating_factors: Accused were of one family, armed, and raised a lalkara to do away with the opposite party; injury to a vital part (stomach) causing death within short time
